- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slightly to avoid overshoot.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.67), model often underestimates; adjust upward to reflect potential rebound.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes — if price spiked recently, forecast should be capped or smoothed to avoid lagged overcorrection.
- Mean reversion bias: if forecast is significantly above recent 5-10 day average, reduce by 5-10% unless sentiment supports continuation.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture late-period sentiment shifts — if sentiment turns positive mid-horizon, adjust forecast upward from that point.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag — forecast should be slightly ahead of historical trend unless sentiment is flat.
